record.original_question: Determine the weight enumerators of cyclic codes whose duals are contained in the Reed–Muller code of order two, especially the cyclic codes whose zeros have the form α^(2^i+2^k), including the cases that appear to share the 3-error-correcting BCH weight enumerator.

evidence.quote: We do not know the weight enumerator of any cyclic code whose zeros have the form α^(2^i+2^k); for instance such codes which have the same weight enumerator as the 3-error-correcting BCH code are not yet characterized (see [144]).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $m\ge 3$ and let $\alpha$ be a primitive element of the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{2^m}$, so that $n=2^m-1$. For integers $i,k\ge 0$, consider the binary cyclic code $C(i,k)$ of length $n$ whose zeros are the conjugates of $\alpha^{2^i+2^k}$ (i.e. the cyclic code whose defining set is the union of the 2-cyclotomic cosets modulo $n$ containing $2^i+2^k$). Equivalently, the dual of $C(i,k)$ is a subcode of the second-order Reed–Muller code $\mathrm{RM}(2,m)$.

(a) Determine the weight enumerator $W_{C(i,k)}(x,y)=\sum_{c\in C(i,k)} x^{n-\mathrm{wt}(c)} y^{\mathrm{wt}(c)}$ of $C(i,k)$ for all admissible pairs $(i,k)$ as a function of $m,i,k$.

(b) In particular, classify all triples $(m,i,k)$ such that the cyclic code with zeros $\alpha,\alpha^{2^i+2^k}$ (together with $\alpha^3$ when appropriate, giving a code of designed minimum distance comparable to the 3-error-correcting primitive narrow-sense binary BCH code of length $n$) has the same weight enumerator as that 3-error-correcting BCH code, and compute the weight enumerator explicitly.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results are known: Kasami (1971) and Bracken–Helleseth (2009) identified families of 3-error-correcting cyclic codes with zero sets {1, 2^ℓ+1, 2^{3ℓ}+1} and {1, 2^ℓ+1, 2^{2ℓ}+1} (gcd(ℓ,m)=1) that share the weight distribution of the 3-error-correcting BCH code, verified for small m. Subsequent work (e.g. on triple-error-correcting cyclic codes from Gold and Kasami–Welch APN functions) has determined further weight distributions of specific subfamilies. However, a complete determination of the weight enumerators of all cyclic codes with zeros of the form α^{2^i+2^k}, and a full characterization of those sharing the 3-error-correcting BCH weight enumerator, remains open in general.

status_evidence.title: On the Triple-Error-Correcting Cyclic Codes with Zero Set {1, 2^i+1, 2^j+1}
status_evidence.snippet: Kasami and Bracken–Helleseth showed certain such codes are 3-error correcting with same weight distribution as BCH for m<14.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results identify families with matching weight distribution; full classification not established.

status_evidence.title: A Triple-Error-Correcting Cyclic Code from the Gold and Kasami-Welch APN Power Functions
status_evidence.snippet: Weight distributions determined for specific triple-error-correcting cyclic codes from APN power functions.

status_evidence.title: Open problems on cyclic codes (Charpin survey)
status_evidence.snippet: States the weight enumerators of cyclic codes with zeros α^{2^i+2^k} are unknown in general.
status_evidence.claim: Problem listed as open in survey on cyclic codes.
